brief: A small-parts organizer with at least six separate bins.

requirements.evidence: The half-depth bins with dividers suit small parts. Every compartment holds a pile of M3 screws, nuts or standoffs (prop:1–15), and all are visible from above.

There are 6 separate lift-out bins, one per base: bin:0,0,0, bin:1,0,0 and bin:2,0,0 (3 compartments each), plus bin:-1,1,0, bin:0,1,0 and bin:1,1,0 (2 compartments each). That gives 15 compartments in total.

finish.summary: I built a 6-cell small-parts organizer. Six full hex bases sit in two staggered rows of three, at (0,0), (1,0), (2,0), (-1,1), (0,1) and (1,1). Each base holds its own separate lift-out half-depth bin. The back row has three bins with 3 compartments each and the front row has three bins with 2 compartments each, so there are 6 bins and 15 compartments in all. I capped the 18 open outer faces with solid end caps and bolted the 9 joints between bases so they can't slide apart. That makes 30 parts, about 2.75 kg of filament. To show what it's for, every compartment holds a pile of M3 screws, nuts or standoffs, and the view from above shows all 15. The check passed with no rule issues and the parts don't collide.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
